1 Samuel.name: 2014-07-27 Why Are You Alone? (Pastor Rob McNutt)
transcript: I've been part of this health survey in Canada for years now, for every few years the government
calls me up and they ask me questions about my health and physical and my mental and psychological
health, trying to find me. They ask me all kinds of questions. There's a series of questions
they ask me along this lines. They say, "Do you have anyone to talk to when you're sad? Do you
have anyone who will take care of you when you're sick?" It's several questions along that
line and then they'll ask me to specify us. Is that none of the time, some of the time, most of
the time? Are they all the time? And I always answer these questions all of the time. I always

He's to what?

The 4th generation is to teach, the 3rd generation, the faithful men are to teach others

So we have 4 generations of people in that verse, and even now, we are the product

When you train that pastor elder, they can train and teach a whole congregation.

Isn't that sad?
Doesn't that, for me as a Christian that broke my heart, especially, I'm like, wow, that's

And God, he holds specially pastors, James 3-1, what do we know that verse?

jewelry with sea glass from the Mediterranean. And it's really cool because they walk along the
beaches of the Mediterranean and they pick up the sea glass that once was a perfect item and has
been broken and weathered by the waves and then they repurpose it to make something beautiful again.
So, it's kind of a picture of their life. But it's also a picture of the Christian life,
as well, if you think about it. So, it's kind of a neat way to have them share their story
through that jewelry. And one of them, women, use her profits to start a successful Moroccan
speech business. And the co-op allows the women not only to provide for their families,
but, like I said, build relationships. And they feel like it's community or family. So,
it's a great time to be with them. Oh, and also, these women have actually been to our church
multiple times. And at least in the fellowship hall, they've set foot in our church, which is a huge
deal. When we have Christmas time come around though, come and bring all their ornaments or their
jewelry for people to purchase as gifts. And the first time they were a little nervous stepping
into an evangelical church, but they were immediately welcomed and embraced. And now they're like,
when can we come back? And it's really neat. We've been able to buy some of the Moroccan sweets
with one of the women and share them at our fellowship time. So, it's been a neat testimony for
them to see that. Yeah, so one of the, one of the things that we also love to do from time to time
is have a big Moroccan breakfast. As you can see in the middle picture there, there's a big
spread of food. And they don't mess around when it comes to Moroccan breakfast. They bring out
all the stops. They're kind of in competition with each other. And you are required to take
every single item that is on that table and fill up your plate. Oftentimes, I can barely get anywhere
with not even halfway. So, I bring it all home to Brian, who's so happy that I have all these
leftovers for him to eat. It's not, it's not a joke. I love, and I tell her, like, who made this
find out? Tell her thank you so much for me. And then they'll make me an extra special batch.
Look at that. So, I have all two of your motives. It's working the system there. This stuff is
fantastic. It's fantastic. But yeah, so these are some of the ministries that we have been
involved in. So far in our seven years there. But there are also ways that you can partner with us
in ministry. Next slide. So, of course, pray. We really appreciate prayers in as we were mentioning,
like, we don't want to do anything outside of what God wants us to do. It's hard because we
God's gifted all of us and we can do a lot in our own strength. But we really don't want to be
doing anything that is just good. We want to be doing the things that are bringing glory to his
kingdom, the things that he wants us to be doing. And so, your prayers, our prayers are the things
that keep us on that path and we're thankful that he continues to be faithful to us. The giving
aspect, you know, it's, it's just a part of it. We have to raise support in order to be there,
you know, and so that's, that's it. You guys as a church, we really appreciate your support.
But if you would like to partner with us as an individual, please, like, we have a thing in the back,
you can take our card, sign up for our newsletter and, you know, be a part of our ministry as
an individual or a community. And then the last part, the go part, you know, you seem
probably on a three years running, coming to Malaga. You are all welcome. We love to see people come.
We make it very easy. All you have to do is buy your plane ticket with, you know, few other things.
We'll help you book a hotel. But like, the reality is, like, we will find you an opportunity to
serve. And if you don't like it, we'll find you a different opportunity. But really, for us,
it's just being a part of the stuff that we get to do. It brings our life, our family,
so much joy and the reality for, for other people to step into that. Maybe you've never considered
it, or maybe you thought about it and you just didn't know how to do it. We want to make it easy.
And it's encouraging for us when we see faces from the state show up.
Even if you would just want a vacation and you just want to show up at a church service, all good for us.
Next slide. More things that you could be praying for. These are our specific prayer requests,
as a ministry team, as a couple. We need more people to join us. We are, we're right now.
Our international church, we have great support because we have a lot of folks in the community
who are participating with the church. But the church planting aspect amongst the different
languages is our team effort. And that's right now the team is the two of us.
And so, you know, mobilization takes anywhere from five to seven years. It's a crazy number.
We didn't believe it when we heard it. It took our family five years from commitment
to the field with support raising and saying goodbye well and doing all these things.
So, growing our team, prayer for an increased team. So, that's the, that part. We are launching
when we return to Spain. We leave January 3rd or December 30th. Thank you. And when we get back
two weeks later, our kids start school, two weeks after that, we're receiving some interns from
Liberty. We have five girls from Liberty coming to spend 15 weeks with us. So, we're launching a
vision trip program. Short-term trips, internships, and residencies. These are all opportunities
for us to bring people to what we're doing. We hope that they find a heart to serve
Jesus in this capacity and maybe stay with us. The next one is, we packed up our house and put it
in storage unit. We wanted to be good stewards with the resources that God has gifted us with.
And so, we didn't want to pay rent for the security of having a home to go back to.
A little bit crazy. The more we think about it. But we're trusting God. We know he'll provide.
Our kids start school literally eight days after we arrive and the interns come 15 days after
we arrive. So, prayer for that. We know that he's got it sorted. We just don't know what it looks
like yet. Next one, of course, that, oh, anacar. Not to pile on. But we were encouraged to buy a new
car when we first went to the field because of the challenges of navigating life using a mechanic
and all that stuff. And we're a single car family. We were big, big family, five people. So,
we couldn't really afford a new car. So, we went with a used car. All those things are starting
to play out seven years in. And so, our car no longer can make it into the city center because of
its eco sticker. But we're praying for a vehicle. And so, you know, if God puts it on your heart,
hey, you know, we want to give the Lucas's a million dollars for a car.
Joking, yeah, nobody needs a million dollars. Next one, of course, our finances. I've shared that
enough. Salvation. So, a lot of these people that we've been working with, right before we left,
we really started seeing like some traction with some folks. And it was really hard to walk away.
And some of these relationships were still maintaining stateside. So, we're looking forward to
returning and seeing, you know, the possibility of some of these people saying yes to Jesus. So,
just pray for some of those relationships that we've started and maintained.
Growth for our church and growth for the opportunity to see fellowships started amongst folks'
heart languages. So, we're looking for actively looking for an Arabic-speaking pastor
in, you know, other languages as well. But right now, that's our first focus. So, if we could see
a Bible study or somebody translate our messages, that might be the first path for us.
And then lastly for our kids. When we came, we were coming for six months and we got our kids
plugged into American school. We prayed that they would be okay and that they would enjoy America.
Truth is, they're enjoying it a little bit too much. And we're so grateful, but our middle
daughter, our oldest daughter, is going to Liberty. So, she's not coming back with us. Our middle
daughter, she's 16. She is scheming on how she can stay in America. One more semester at American
High School. She was so looking forward to homecoming, riding the bus, all the American stuff.
Our middle son was like, "Dad, is there going to be bullies?" I'm like, "There might be." But they
are thriving. They're loving it. And yeah, just prayers that they will recognize that going home
with us is the right thing. Because we're taking a regardless. I just don't want to be heartbroken.
All right, next slide. So, one thing we've learned during our time in ministry is though it is a
wonderful thing to help the needy, the displays, and show the love of Jesus to the unbeliever.
If we leave out the most important component of actually opening our mouths and sharing
the why behind the hands and feet of Jesus, then we've completely missed it.
The whole point of everything we do is bringing glory to God and pointing the loss to Jesus.
They're Savior. It's so important to not only show them, but tell them. I'm going to close with
a few passages, Romans 10, 13 through 15, "For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved,
how then can they call on the one they have not believed in? And how can they believe in the
one of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone preaching to them? And how
can anyone preach unless they are sent? As it is written, how beautiful are the feet of those who
bring good news? We all have the responsibility and privilege to share the good news with those
around us, whether it's in our community or work or friends. We all have an opportunity to be a part
of God's great commission. I love the message that you have over the back of your door.
You are now entering the mission field. That is so true. I love that. And we want to thank you,
Faith Bible, for being a part of our story and for sending us and doing what that passage says.
So thank you for being an encouragement to our family over the years. One more, one more scripture.
This is something that I look forward to this day. In this day, you will say, give praise to the
Lord, proclaim his name, make known among the nations what he has done, and proclaim that his name
is exalted. Sing to the Lord for he has done glorious things. Let this be known to all the world. Amen.
Sure. After I'm going to pray, and then afterwards, we have a table set up back there,
as she mentioned, there's some of those crafty things that the ladies made. You're welcome to buy
any of those things. We have prayer cards back there. There's a thing you can sign up with your email.
If you want to be on our email list. So let me just pray. Father, we thank you again for this
relationship with Faith Bible. We really appreciate just their coming alongside us. And Lord,
we thank you just for the opportunity that we get to do what we're doing. Lord, we just want to
pray for the many lost that have yet to know you. And we just want to pray for these future
opportunities. We pray, Lord, that you'll continue to grow and stretch Faith Bible Church's heart
to serve the least reached in Jesus name. Amen.

I remember my first bike, it was a baby blue,
hand me down, girls, bikes, someone gave our family.

Kind of looked like this one right here, except for it was more faded and more rusted.
I learned to ride it and I was very happy to ride it around with the big kids,
because little kids had tricycles that were slow and lame and you couldn't go any place.
Big kids rode bicycles and when you had a bike you could go anywhere.
We lived in the town of Toronto, Nova Scotia, my sister and I would ride our bikes a couple of blocks to swimming lessons.
And we would take the rider down to the store and get a treat.
And when you had a bike you had freedom.
It was proof that you were all grown up now and you could take care of yourself.
Because when you went on a ride, parents kind of had to let you go.
They didn't really know where you were, you're just riding all around the community somewhere's on your bike.
So I never really thought too much about the fact that my bike was a hand me down girls' bike.
Because if it wasn't for that hand me down bike I wouldn't have had any bike at all.
I did remember that dad gave it a facelift, he got a can of black spray paint and he sprayed the frame.
And he was like, oh, that's like a brand new bike now.
Wow, that was good.

My grandmother had a neighbor whose son was a year older than me and once a year I would receive a couple of bags of clothes that the kid had grown out of and gave my grandmother and she gave it to me.
And I remember being always so excited to see what new clothes I had got didn't really care that they were hand me down.
They were new to me.
And I remember very specifically one time this was when velour shirts and corduroids were in.
I remember some of you don't have any clue what a velour shirt is and some of you are laughing because you're visualizing me in a wide-collar velour shirt with corduroids on, right?

When you fear God,
you stop being impressed with yourself.
You stop living for human approval.
You start living for the one who's opinion actually matters.

but the fear of God it cultivates it.

you finally see life for as it really is.
You stop pretending you're in control.
You stop treating your sin lightly.
You stop treating God casually.
The fear of the Lord is the starting point
for all right thinking.

you generally in ignorance and arrogance,
barrel head first into self destruction.
